usage: Very frequent — the most Mozartian ornament
intent: A sigh: the dissonance leans into the resolution

usage: Moderate — at phrase peaks and cadences
intent: Grace, elegance — the melodic equivalent of a smile

usage: At cadences, especially on penultimate note
intent: Anticipation before resolution — the held breath before arrival
Tenderness — the approach is as important as the arrival
The character speaks alone — the most personal moment

common_choice: Grace note from below
why: Mimics a singer's intake of breath before the first word

common_choice: Appoggiatura (lean-resolve)
why: Dissonance on strong beat creates longing before the peak

what_moment_needs: Fill silence; keep the line alive
common_choice: Turn group around held note
why: Mimics a singer's vibrato or melismatic turn; the note breathes

common_choice: Trill on supertonic
why: Dominant tension sustained and released at resolution

common_choice: Chromatic neighbor sigh
why: Half-step dissonance = most intimate, most painful interval

common_choice: Scalar or arpeggiated flourish
why: Fills silence with directional motion toward next phrase

common_choice: Add ornaments absent from first statement
why: Ornamented return = the character has grown; bare original = innocence

common_choice: Escape tone or unexpected leap after V
why: The ornament "misses" the expected resolution — surprise through misdirection

common_choice: Fragmenting ornaments, slowing
why: Full turn → half-turn → single grace → bare note: the ornament dissolves

common_choice: NO ornament — deliberate nakedness
why: Stripping ornaments where expected creates more power than adding them

common_choice: Occasional gentle grace note, simple neighbor
why: One grace per 8-bar phrase; let the melody breathe

common_choice: Appoggiaturas (sighing), gentle turns, portamento
why: Appoggiatura on the most tender word/note of each phrase

common_choice: Rapid turns, mordents, quick ascending grace notes
why: Turns at phrase peaks; mordents on strong beats; everything dances

common_choice: Written-out chromatic ornaments, arpeggiated flourishes, wide-span grace groups
why: Chopin-style filigree; the ornament IS the melody's emotional content

common_choice: Slow appoggiaturas, suspensions, chromatic neighbors, descending sighs
why: Each appoggiatura is a wound; the dissonance lingers before resolving

common_choice: Trills, tremolo, rapid mordents, nervous repeated notes
why: Trills that don't resolve cleanly; tremolo that builds without release

common_choice: Written-out trills as texture, broad cadential flourishes, fanfare grace notes
why: Cadential trills at structural arrivals; grace notes announce, not whisper

common_choice: Either stark bare notes (frozen terror) or frantic over-ornamentation (panic)
why: Choose one extreme: the music is either paralyzed or hysterical

common_choice: Fragments of earlier ornaments, simplified versions
why: Quote an ornament from an earlier section, but incomplete — as if remembered imperfectly

common_choice: Wide-spaced arpeggiated chords, bell-like grace notes, high harmonics
why: Bell sonority; high sustained notes with occasional ethereal grace
